summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would shorten the default bankruptcy period from three years to one year, while extending income contribution obligations beyond discharge.
Income contribution assessment would generally run for three years from bankruptcy, with people whose incomes exceed the threshold liable after their earlier discharge.
The changes would begin six months after Royal Assent and cover existing bankruptcies, with longer periods preserved where an objection to discharge has extended bankruptcy.
changes: People liable for income contributions would have 10 business days to notify trustees of changes to their contact details.
Duties to keep and produce financial records would extend to the contribution period after discharge.
Supervised bank account arrangements could continue after discharge to collect outstanding contributions.
Trustees and the Official Receiver would retain the ability to object to automatic discharge.
summary.affected: Bankrupt people, discharged people with contribution obligations, creditors, trustees and the Official Receiver would be affected.
